report.title: SPY short-put comparison: income versus assignment obligation
report.period_basis: Historical option snapshot and scenario analysis
report.provenance: Approved redacted summary of the dated private report. Original account evidence is not published.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: The higher-premium package carried a much larger purchase obligation. The two historical sell-to-open tickets compared one SPY US$700 put with ten SPY US$600 puts. They were order illustrations, not confirmed executions, and the maturities differed.

sections.heading: Visual 1: Side-by-side contract table
sections.body:
| Measure | Strategy A: one US$700 put | Strategy B: ten US$600 puts |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Expiry | 26 February 2027 | 31 December 2026 |
| Days shown on the original ticket | 115 | 58 |
| Assumed premium per share | US$12.19 | US$1.88 |
| Maximum gross premium | US$1,219 | US$1,880 |
| Shares if all assigned | 100 | 1,000 |
| Gross assignment obligation | US$70,000 | US$600,000 |
| Expiry break-even per share | US$687.81 | US$598.12 |
| Maximum option loss if SPY reaches zero | US$68,781 | US$598,120 |
| Premium / full assignment obligation | 1.7414% | 0.3133% |

Chart: pair gross premium bars with separate assignment-obligation bars. Use separate labelled axes so the additional US$661 premium is not visually confused with the additional US$530,000 obligation.

sections.heading: What the comparison means
sections.body:
Strategy A was an ownership-oriented illustration; Strategy B was a leveraged premium-harvesting illustration. The first structure requires willingness and funding to buy 100 shares at the strike. The ten-put structure can create a US$600,000 purchase obligation even when the initial buying-power requirement is much lower.

The reported tenor for Strategy B was 58 days, not roughly 40 days. Preserve the 31 December 2026 expiry and the ticket's displayed day count. Do not compare the two premiums as though they were earned over the same period.

sections.heading: Visual 2: Downside payoff table
sections.body:
| SPY at each option's own expiry | Strategy A P/L | Strategy B P/L |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| US$700 | +US$1,219 | +US$1,880 |
| US$650 | -US$3,781 | +US$1,880 |
| US$600 | -US$8,781 | +US$1,880 |
| US$550 | -US$13,781 | -US$48,120 |
| US$500 | -US$18,781 | -US$98,120 |

Chart: labelled payoff lines, with an explicit warning that the expiries differ. These are terminal scenarios, not interim option marks.

sections.heading: Risks and limits
sections.body:
Buying-power effect is not maximum loss and is not guaranteed to remain fixed. A fall in SPY or a rise in implied volatility can increase short-option losses and margin demands before expiry. Early assignment and forced liquidation are possible.

All returns are conditional and before costs. The original quote reference was SPY US$751.96. The assumed limit premiums do not prove that either trade filled. The report makes no claim about current availability, current pricing or personal account balances.
